items.title: I Think IBM Stock Will Be Higher in 5 Years. I Still Wouldn't Buy It Today.
items.summary: Following a brutal 2026, the five-year case comes down to reaccelerating software growth and a 31-year dividend streak.

items.title: IBM Has Raised Its Dividend for 31 Years. Inflation Is Still Winning
items.summary: IBM has raised its dividend for three decades straight, but the latest increase fits on a penny. Before counting on that income to keep pace with rising costs, retirees should understand what the streak actually delivers.

items.summary: Investors need something that evolves with a changing economy.

items.title: IBM Once Held Nvidia's Spot as Tech's Biggest Name. The Stock Just Crashed 25%. Here's the Comeback Case.
items.summary: IBM stock fell 25% after a weak Q2. Here's why Red Hat, hybrid cloud, and a 31-year dividend streak keep its comeback case alive.

items.title: IONQ Stock Surges On Tech Wins, But The Heavy Burn Persists
items.summary: IonQ (IONQ) shares rose 9.5% on Thursday, closing at $40.34 after six sessions that had mostly gone the other way. The reason on offer was research: quantum algorithms running inside mainstream engineering software, developed with Synopsys, sped up complex industrial design by up to 14.6%. That is genuine progress. It is also not a sale, and the price you pay for IonQ already assumes a great many sales.

items.title: Is Accenture Stock Cheap, Or Is Its Operating Margin At A Peak?
items.summary: Accenture (ACN) stock has gone down for a year while the market has gone up. At around $190, it sits toward the cheap end of its own ten-year history on earnings. The risk sits in what those earnings are made of.

items.title: Should You Buy NetApp Stock For The Shares It Keeps Retiring?
items.summary: NetApp (NTAP) has spent years quietly retiring its own stock while the attention went to its flash arrays and AI deals. The stock is not quiet now: it has gained about 92% over the trailing six months and sits roughly 5% below its 52-week high. Fewer shares mean each one carries more of the profit. The question is what that is worth at this price.

items.title: Inside the Trump Administration’s $215 Million Bet to Win the Quantum Arms Race
items.summary: The U.S. Energy Department launches Quantum Genesis Q, a competition to build an error-corrected, ‘scientifically relevant’ quantum computer.
